Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

variation noun

also variations, vary, variety (change), fluctuation, ups and downs

classical

Cic. Fam. 5.12.4: temporum varietātēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. vicissitūdō)
Publil. Sent. I 10

varietās, varietātis f.

noun, third declension

variation, change; variety

The general word for things that differ or change: of weather, fortune, colour or food. It also means variety, a range of things (see range).

Other words

  • vicissitūdō, vicissitūdinis f. — alternation, change by turns

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.16: diērum noctiumque vicissitūdinēs (Lewis & Short); Ter. Eun. 276: omnium rērum, heus, vicissitūdō est

    Change that comes round in turn: day and night, the seasons, taking turns in talk (Cic. Off. 1.134).

  • variātiō, variātiōnis f. — a difference, variation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 24.9.3: sine variātiōne ūllā (Lewis & Short)

    Rare: Lewis & Short cites only Livy, of a vote taken without any difference among the centuries.

Examples

  • Jūcundum nīl est, nisi quod reficit varietās.

    Nothing is pleasant unless variety freshens it.Publil. Sent. I 10

See also range, difference, change.
